key_insight: World Action Models can do more than predict actions: they can also generate future visual observations. This paper turns that capability into Recurrent Generative Replay (REGEN), letting robots rehearse old skills with synthetic pseudo-trajectories instead of storing human demonstrations.
problem_solved: Continual imitation learning usually suffers from catastrophic forgetting, because a robot forgets earlier tasks when learning new ones. A major bottleneck is the need to keep past human demonstration data, which can be costly, limited, or unavailable for replay.
method: Use a World Action Model (WAM) as a generative simulator that predicts both actions and future observations.
Recursively query the WAM to synthesize pseudo-replay trajectories for previously learned tasks.
Train the policy with these generated replays during continual adaptation, reducing reliance on stored human demonstrations.
impact: REGEN offers a practical path to lifelong robot learning without retaining large demonstration datasets. For AI/ML practitioners, it shows how generative world models can support memory-efficient continual learning and reduce forgetting.
